title: Send the gateway the charge the cardholder agreed to

blocks.text: Your switch now takes purchases from a bank's terminals in Germany, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Chile and Kuwait, and forwards them to a REST gateway as `POST /charges`. Finance has found charges that don't match what cardholders signed for, and the gateway's operator has sent back requests it says should never have reached it.
`ChargeMapper.toCharge` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/ChargeMapper.java` builds each `Charge` from a terminal's 1987 request. It is written except for three methods marked `TODO`:

items: `kind`: the gateway knows two kinds, `"sale"` and `"refund"`;
`amount`: the amount as the gateway reads it, a decimal number in the request's currency. The currencies in the gateway's contract are in `ACCEPTED`;
`localTime`: the terminal's local date and time of the purchase, as the gateway's reports and date checks will read it.

blocks.text: `toCharge` is called with the moment of mapping and the terminal's time zone, so that the tests can map requests at any moment of the year. A request the gateway can't take is refused with an `ISOException` and never sent. About ten lines in total.

cases.says: a euro purchase becomes a sale charge with its decimal amount, its currency and its full local date and time
a pound refund becomes a refund charge
the currency's exponent places the decimal point: none for Chilean pesos, three for Kuwaiti dinars
a currency outside the gateway's list is refused, even one jPOS knows, such as 999 or 840
a purchase from 29 December mapped on 3 January keeps the old year
a purchase stamped just after midnight on 1 January, mapped seconds before midnight, gets the new year
the transaction type decides the kind, whatever account types the processing code names
a cash advance, a transfer or a cash-back purchase is refused rather than sent as a sale

origin.section: 12.4. A Value With No Entry in the Table Is Refused, Never Guessed

concepts: Field 4 is minor units and the currency in field 49 places the decimal point; amounts stay BigDecimal, and only the gateway's own list of currencies is accepted.
Processing codes map on their transaction type through an explicit table, and a type the table lacks is refused rather than sent as a sale.
A date without a year takes the year that puts it nearest to a clock passed in, so a delayed advice keeps last year and a fast terminal's message at New Year gets the new one.
